name: meeple-loop-orchard-draw-three-v1
description: ⚠️ 09/09/2026, THE COMMONS FLIP: THIS ARM NOW PINS THE PASSENGERS AS WELL. Dean ruled the commons in as the engine DEFAULT (docs/commons-handoff-2026-09-09-v1.md), which moved four leaves at once - rules.turn.visitCurrency to 'commons', rules.turn.bonusTiming to 'start', rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour to 0, and the Orchard door's printed draw to 2/2. An overlay that pins only what it is named for stops being the arm it is called, silently, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson written down: NAME THE PASSENGERS BEFORE RULING AN ARM IN. So the `set` below carries every leaf this arm's game relied on, whether or not it was in the original experiment. ⭐ 05/09/2026: DEAN RULED R17 IN AND THE ENGINE DEFAULTS MOVED WITH IT. The shipped game is now meepleAsCard true, meepleAsCardGoesTo 'board', slotToll 1 and meepleCapPerColour 2, which is exactly overlays/meeple-on-board-v1.overlay.json. ⚠️ SO THIS OVERLAY NOW PINS THE v1 LOOP EXPLICITLY (meepleAsCard false, slotToll null, meepleCapPerColour 1) on top of its own knob, because it is the Orchard door sweep of the v1 LOOP and the default is no longer that loop. Its own sweep value still wins over the pin. The equivalent sweep under the SHIPPED rules is overlays/meeple-on-board-cap-one-v1.overlay.json and -cap-three- for the cap; the others have no R17 twin yet. THE ORCHARD EXCEPTION, RE-ASKED UNDER THE NEW CURRENCY, and it is a CONTROL rather than a proposal. Under v31 the Orchard door was the one printed exception in the door set: Draw 3 where plain would be Draw 2. The exception existed for one reason and one only, the self-cancellation law - a visit cost the visitor a card, and the bonus slot's other option was a free Draw 1, so a Draw 2 door cost 1 and returned 2 for a net +1, exactly what the free option gave for nothing, making it strictly worse than its own alternative. THE MEEPLE LOOP DISSOLVES BOTH HALVES OF THAT ARGUMENT. A visit now costs no card at all, so there is nothing to cancel, and the free standalone Draw 1 is deleted, so there is no alternative for the door to be worse than. The shipped arm therefore takes the exception away and runs red at a plain Draw 2. This overlay puts it back at 3, and its job is to say how much of any measured traffic to the red door is the design and how much is simply the biggest number on the table. THE PREDICTION IF THE ARM IS HEALTHY: putting red back to 3 should move the door mix noticeably toward red and move the HOOK barely at all, because under the meeple loop a visit is free and a seat visits whatever its held colours and the open slots allow, not whatever pays best. THE PREDICTION IF THE ARM IS NOT: if red at 3 lifts the hook materially, then visits are still being chosen on payout arithmetic rather than on availability, the loop has not actually become a circuit, and the door values need pricing rather than the currency needing changing. That is the more interesting of the two results. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) door mix by colour, red's share against the shipped arm; (2) the hook, which should be close to flat; (3) cards drawn per turn and the hand-limit discard rate, the sanity check that the arm did what it says and the check that a fatter draw is not simply overflowing a hand of 7; (4) the wild share, because a richer red makes red the target colour a pair is most often spent to buy. DO NOT READ THIS AS A BALANCE PROPOSAL. Under the meeple loop every door is the plain suit action, which is a rule Dean has ruled twice, and reinstating an exception needs a stronger reason than a door mix that looks tidier. PATH NOTE (engine, 04/09/2026): the arm reads workers.roster.draw.drawUnderMeepleCurrency, a SECOND printed payload, and never workers.roster.draw.draw - which still carries the shipped 3/3 and drives the 'card' control. Writing the old path here would validate, apply, and change nothing under the arm, which is the inert-knob signature this project has already paid for once. ⚠️ STATUS, 04/09/2026: the meeple loop is now the shipped default, so the visitCurrency line in this overlay's `set` is redundant and is left in place as self-documentation. The overlay survives as a named variant, and its subject is settled rather than open: Draw 3 against Draw 2 moved the hook not at all (0.37 both) and the door mix by one point, so the Orchard exception is retired and red is a plain Draw 2 in the shipped game. Run this to re-open that, not to tune it. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved. ⚠️ 13/09/2026: rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed true and rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats.2 1 are pinned here because the shipped defaults flipped when the commons was deleted, so this arm stays the game it was. ⛔ DELIVERY MEEPLE PINNED 14/09/2026: Dean ruled the delivery meeple ON as the shipped default (rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace 1, meepleSpendTiming 'afterAction', meepleSpendPerTurn 1, meepleSpendDistinctColours false) together with two new island rules, the space choice (rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice true: a delivery names either free space) and the closing draw (rules.turn.closingDrawPerCrate 1: filling a tile draws one card per crate). This overlay predates it, so all six leaves are pinned here BY NAME at their pre-ruling values (deliveryMeepleSpace null, meepleSpendTiming 'start', meepleSpendPerTurn null, meepleSpendDistinctColours false, deliverySpaceChoice false, closingDrawPerCrate 0; 'start' and null are the old inert values, not 'none' and 0) and it still replays its own game. Since 16/09/2026 the balloons, the Aerodrome, the Village Store, the closing draw and the wild substitution are deleted from the engine, so this overlay no longer replays the game it was recorded on. Its pins for the balloons and the Aerodrome, the Village Store and the closing draw were removed with them. ⚠️ 16/09/2026, THE TOKEN ISLAND AND THE TURN-ORDER RULINGS: the island is now two tokens per tile (Dean, R3: a first delivery pays both demands and chooses its token, a second pays the last token plus 2 any; Workers sit on the 3 and 4 VP tokens), and the Vegetable and Dairy boards were retexted (R9, R10), so this overlay's pins of rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice, rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace were removed with the delivery spaces. It pins rules.economy.noticeBoardPower.vegetableWildCards 0 and dairyDiscount 0 by name; under visitCurrency 'meeple' its island meeples now sit on the 3 and 4 VP tokens, and it now starts with seat 0 and gives one more turn each (rules.setup.firstPlayer 'seat0', rules.endGame.endOfGame 'oneMoreTurnEach'). It no longer replays the game it was recorded on, and nothing measured before 16/09/2026 is comparable as a level.
